# How to Use This Book {.unnumbered}

This textbook is structured as a **Systems Blueprint and Architectural Reference**. It is designed to guide you through assembling, measuring, constraining, and qualifying a complete physical AI machine from scratch.

All supplementary materials, interactive models, hardware lab contracts, and curriculum blueprints are maintained online at [**`physical.mlsysbook.ai`**](https://physical.mlsysbook.ai).

---

## The Anatomy of a Physical AI Agent

Rather than teaching disconnected algorithms, every chapter in this book installs and validates one vital organ of the autonomous physical agent across three foundational parts:

### Part I: Foundations (The Laws of Physical Computing)
* **Chapter 1: Physical Causality** — System boundaries, momentum, and irreversible physical state mutation ($W_t \to W_{t+1}$).
* **Chapter 2: Time and Latency** — Sensory freshness decay ($\Delta t$), tail latency budgets ($P_{99}$), and dynamic stopping distances ($d_{\text{stop}}$).
* **Chapter 3: Multi-Rate Systems** — Proposal–permission cadence decoupling, lock-free IPC, and MCU watchdog crash containment.

### Part II: Agent Architecture (The Proposal–Permission Organs)
* **Chapter 4: Perception** — Photons to DMA taxes, ViT spatial tokenization, and multi-sensor time synchronization.
* **Chapter 5: Memory** — Temporal belief, $SE(3)$ coordinate frame graphs, and latent world models (JEPAs).
* **Chapter 6: Reasoning** — 1 Hz Vision-Language Model semantic goal grounding and expiring intent leases ($t_{\text{expire}}$).
* **Chapter 7: Planning** — 20–50 Hz Vision-Language-Action trajectory chunking and $\mathcal{C}^2$ jerk-continuous ensembling.
* **Chapter 8: Reflex** — 1 kHz MCU mathematical safety barriers ($\Pi_{\mathcal{U}_{\text{safe}}}$), dynamic stopping vetoes, and category fallbacks.

### Part III: Integration & Release (Governed Deployment)
* **Chapter 9: Placement** — Heterogeneous silicon placement maps and whole-system resource ledgers (FLOPs, SRAM, Watts, CAN bus QoS).
* **Chapter 10: Governance** — Bumpless human takeover state machines, cryptographic provenance logging, and policy endogeneity mitigation.
* **Chapter 11: Assurance** — Operational Design Domain (ODD) boundaries, STPA hazard matrices, and Claim-Argument-Evidence (CAE) safety cases.
* **Chapter 12: Capstone Defense** — Full-system integration under unannounced seeded bench faults and release verdict sign-off.

All firmware skeletons, FreeRTOS harnesses, and automated test suites are accessible via [**`physical.mlsysbook.ai/labs`**](https://physical.mlsysbook.ai):

| **`01`** | **Closing the Causal Loop:** Advisory vs. Actuating mode and world mutation ($W_{t+1}$) | `LOOP-01` |
| **`02`** | **The Freshness Wall:** Sensory decay ($\Delta t$) and stopping bounds ($d_{\text{stop}}$) | `REQ-01` |
| **`03`** | **Metrology on Silicon:** Complete-path $P_{99}$ latency profiler and bus contention | `REQ-01` |
| **`04`** | **Multi-Rate Fault Containment:** Lock-free SRAM IPC and surviving MPU panics | `RUN-01` |
| **`05`** | **Perception Frontier:** Pre-inference DMA tax and 3D spatial tokenizers | `OBS-01` |
| **`06`** | **Temporal Belief & Drift:** $SE(3)$ frame trees and state validity TTL leases | `STATE-01` |
| **`07`** | **Two-Speed Intent:** MPU VLM grounding and expiring intent leases ($t_{\text{expire}}$) | `INTENT-01` |
| **`08`** | **MCU Real-Time Enforcer:** 1 kHz bare-metal CBF projection ($\Pi_{\mathcal{U}_{\text{safe}}}$) | `ENF-01` |
| **`09`** | **Placement Ripple:** Heterogeneous resource ledgers (FLOPs, SRAM, Watts, bus QoS) | `PLACE-01` |
| **`10`** | **Shadow Mode & Logging:** Passive shadow execution and PTP telemetry logs | `AUTH-01` |
| **`11`** | **Authority Paths:** Bumpless joystick takeover and OTA firmware rollback | `AUTH-01` |
| **`12`** | **The Learning Turn:** Policy endogeneity filtering and governed fine-tuning | `REL-01` |
| **`13`** | **Ship Gate Defense:** Cross-layer fault injection and Claim-Argument-Evidence case | `REL-01` |
| **`Capstone`** | **Oral Capstone Defense:** Live defense under unannounced seeded bench faults | **Final Release** |

## The Cumulative Design Dossier

In traditional engineering courses, students write a free-form final report after the project is already finished.

In this curriculum, you build an accumulating, versioned **Cumulative Design Dossier** that evolves chapter-by-chapter. Every chapter freezes a specific, checkable engineering artifact:

| Chapter | Capability Installed | Dossier Artifact Produced |
| :---: | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | System Boundary and Causal Scope | `Loop Charter` (`LOOP-01`) |
| **2** | Dynamic Deadlines and Latency Budgets | `Requirements and Assumptions Ledger` (`REQ-01`) |
| **3** | Multi-Rate Scheduling and Fault Isolation | `Continuous Runtime Skeleton` (`RUN-01`) |
| **4** | Sensory Acquisition and Bus Priorities | `Observation Contract` (`OBS-01`) |
| **5** | Spatial State and Uncertainty Horizons | `State, Frames and Timing Model` (`STATE-01`) |
| **6** | Semantic Goal Grounding and Intent | `Policy Interface and Intent Schema` (`INTENT-01`) |
| **7** | Continuous Trajectory Rollouts | `Planning and Trajectory Schema` (`PLAN-01`) |
| **8** | Real-Time Physical Limits and Vetoes | `Action Limits and Enforcement Design` (`ENF-01`) |
| **9** | Silicon Resource Allocation | `Placement Map and Resource Ledger` (`PLACE-01`) |
| **10** | Human Overrides and Provenance Logging | `Human-Authority and Governed Data Record` (`AUTH-01`) |
| **11** | ODD Qualification and CAE Safety Case | `Integrated Deployment Case` (`REL-01`) |

At the end of the journey, your completed dossier forms the empirical basis for rendering a formal **Deploy**, **Condition** (deploy with restricted operating bounds), or **Refuse** release verdict.

---

## The Three Ways to Use This Material

1. **For University Cohorts (e.g., ETH Zurich Project Seminar / Harvard):**
   * Follow the 14-week schedule in `course/syllabus.md`.
   * Complete the core physical hardware milestones on the Physical AI Kit.
   * Present at the Midterm Design Review (T3) and defend your final dossier under instructor-seeded faults at the Final Defense (T5).
2. **For Self-Learners and Kit Builders:**
   * Work through Chapters 1 to 12 at your own pace with the Arduino UNO Q on your desk.
   * Use the tested starter checkpoints in `labs/` so a bug in one section never blocks you from progressing.
3. **For Practicing Engineers:**
   * Use the individual chapters as modular systems contracts for architecting real-world autonomous systems, quadrotors, rovers, or robotic manipulators.
